description: Choose at most k distinct projects. A project requires its capital threshold and adds its profit to your current capital. Maximize final capital.
examples:
Input: k = 2, w = 0, profits = [1,2,3], capital = [0,1,1]
Output: 4
intuition: Sort projects by required capital. Put affordable profits in a max-heap and take the largest profit, then add any projects made affordable by it.
approach: Sort projects by required capital. Put affordable profits in a max-heap and take the largest profit, then add any projects made affordable by it.
explanation: Sort projects by required capital. Put affordable profits in a max-heap and take the largest profit, then add any projects made affordable by it.

timeComplexityBreakdown.variables: n = projects; K = min(k, n) = maximum projects that can be selected.

phases.label: Push each affordable project at most once

simplifications: O(n + n log n + n log n + K log n)
timeComplexityBreakdown.note: K ≤ n, so all selections fit within O(n log n). The next pointer prevents scanning all projects again on every selection.
